title: fix(plugin-sharing)!: every share grant counts; the sharing scopes carry the share-grant leaf instead of a list capped at 5,000 (ADR-0155 step 6)
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibyXo4gSy8DJPNz4ANz
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao8mXHQniWvfYM2uHoosm2Da)_

Fixes #33787

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: updated here

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:开了按记录共享的对象上,成员此前最多只算五千条共享给他的记录,合并后每一条都算;放在另一个数据源、或存储不能在库内核对共享的对象(内存、MongoDB、OData 三类)上,共享不再生效,新建共享和共享规则会被明确拒绝,启动时点名;为共享表按名挂了读取拦截的部署会拒绝启动;PostgreSQL 上一条共享都没有的成员,列表总数会变慢(十万行约 1.5 毫秒到 7.3 毫秒,百万行约 7.9 毫秒到 42 毫秒,翻页本身不变,SQLite 不受影响),后续卡 #36034 去实测一种可能让总数重新走索引的写法。
- 为什么做:这是「共享范围改走库内子查询」这组改动的收尾一步,替在同一对象上持有大量共享的成员解决静默少看:持有六千条共享的成员今天只看得到其中五千条,打开没算进去的那条显示不存在。
- 出错会怎样:若这一步出错,受影响的是开了共享的对象的列表、计数和详情(可能多看或少看);本次不改任何存储数据,撤回这次合并即可恢复。
- 要你做的:这次改动修订了共享那篇架构决策记录,并收紧了上面说的两类部署的行为,需要你本人批准后才能合并。

## What changes

ADR-0155 plan step 6, the switch. Steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 are merged, as are #35906, #35946 and #35952 (Oracle `RAW(16)`, PR #36001). This branch is the local build replayed by cherry-pick onto main 78437e20d7, with patch-ids identical commit for commit (`git range-diff`: 6 of 6 `=`). The readings below name the local commits, built on c00be39b74: 6f658cd302→6b71a89a1d, a246e87044→8c94ebc0e6, 57e0485c08→60865ad7d6, 9e7a65585e→56a0828d3e, 28dbd3fdf1→76a4bc74f2, f789fb96e2→53f788e776. Between the two bases, main changed plugin-security (#36085, viewAllFields); overlap-check against 78437e20d7 is clean, and this head's CI is the reading of record. Round 4, which answers contract review 7064569198, adds one commit built on this branch, 4f11b215c3. Its readings are taken at that head. It lands last.

- **The two scopes carry the share-grant leaf** (`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts`). `buildReadFilter` writes `{ $or: [ownerMatch, queueMatch?, { id: { $in: SharedRecordIds.read(object, user) } }, { id: { $in: pendingApprovalIds } }?] }`; `buildWriteFilter` writes the update form with `SharedRecordIds.write(object, user, ['edit', 'full'])` and no approval arm; `delete` stays the owner match alone. The capped grant read (`grantedRecordIds`, `limit 5000`) is gone: no grant is read into memory, nothing binds one parameter per grant, and the pending-approval ids are a disjunct of their own (ruling 6942854600: Q1 A, Q2 the recommended column, Q3 A; ruling 6895275749, root fix only).
- **The AST `filter` mirror is removed** (`sharing-plugin.ts`, the read and bulk-write paths, and, in round 4, the `sys_record_share` self-scope branch): every scope is composed into `where` only, the key the engine's executor seam judges. Pinned: `ctx.ast.filter` is undefined on both paths and on the self-scope's plain-user and principal-less cases (`sharing-service.test.ts`).
- **ADR-0155 ② R2, the storage rows.** `SharingService.shareGrantsInertReason(object)` answers why share grants cannot count on an object: the engine's recognition says `other-datasource`, or the object's driver does not list `SharedRecordIds` in `supports.fixedReadLeaves` (today: driver-memory, driver-mongodb, driver-odata). An engine that cannot say answers null, and the leaf is written. In ADR-0111 D7's inert-grant verdict this arm is asked last, so every refusal that shipped keeps its attribution (a public or phantom-anchored federated object still refuses for that reason); it also stops the public arm's external floor (#25549) from lifting there. Where it answers a reason: neither scope carries the share arm (owner, queue and approval arms unchanged), the edit gate reads no grant, the grant door refuses `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` with the reason (`grantAccess` / `createGrant`, as SYSTEM and as a direct caller), the sharing-rule save door refuses `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` / 422 with the remedy, the boot names at `warn`, once, every such object holding `sys_record_share` rows (`inertShareGrantHolders`, `share-arm-boot.ts#reportInertShareGrantHolders`), and `security/explain` reports each share on such a record as evaluated and `neutral` and says why (`plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts`).
- **ADR-0155 ② R1 at boot, the host row.** A `kernel:bootstrapped` hook in `SharingServicePlugin` asks the engine's own recognition of D4's class, `engine.fixedReadLeafClassOf(SharedRecordIds.read('sys_record_share', probe))`. Class `registration-by-name` (an object-scoped middleware, or a `beforeFind` / `afterFind` hook, for `sys_record_share`) throws the seam's own `fixedReadLeafRefusal`, `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500, naming the registration, before `kernel:listening`. No exemption for a handler that skips system reads. A registration made after boot meets the engine's refusal at read, with the same envelope. A registration naming no object, or `'*'`, is outside the class and is told in the changeset. No new package edge: `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/core` were already dependencies.
- **Test doubles that resolve the leaf.** `plugin-security/src/shared-record-ids-in-memory.testkit.ts` resolves a fixed-read leaf over a double's own `sys_record_share` rows under the leaf's own `fixedInnerReadOf`, once per statement (a faulted share table fails the statement), and throws on a leaf outside an `$in` comparand. `readable-ids-in-memory.testkit.ts` uses it. `plugin-sharing/src/shared-record-ids.testkit.ts` does the same for plugin-sharing's doubles.
- **The texts the switch makes due** (claim amendment 7060526112, seat 7's call 2026-11-21):
  - `docs/adr/0155-...md`: a dated, append-only note (2026-11-21) says `grantedRecordIds` is gone and its filter is now the leaf's blank-id guard, anchored `packages/spec/src/data/fixed-read-leaf.ts#FixedInnerRead`. The grant-read bullet at line 160 named the removed symbol as an anchor; it now names it bare, as D2 does, and the note carries the live anchor. Nothing else in the ADR moves.
  - `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts`, prose only, no type change. The section on the share arm now states the leaf in the present tense ("The read scope's share arm is an engine-internal leaf"), says what the list was before the switch, and says that share grants count only where the leaf can be evaluated: elsewhere no share arm, no grant row read, and the grant and rule doors refuse `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` / 422 (R2). The host bullet compares with what the engine read returned before the switch, and `buildReadFilter`'s and `grant`'s jsdoc say the same.
  - `packages/spec/src/data/fixed-read-leaf-conformance.test.ts`: the D-0 comment that named `grantedRecordIds` now describes the read before the switch and points at the blank-id guard. Comment only.
  - `skills/objectstack-data/rules/datasources.md`: one sentence, made exact in round 4 (N2): "Share grants count only on `sys_record_share`'s datasource under a SQL driver; elsewhere a grant or rule save is refused `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` (422), and a `sharingRules` reconcile aborts on it." The 422 is what the grant door and the rule-save door answer. A rule declared in a stack's `sharingRules` meets no door: its reconcile pass aborts on the same code, in the log. Paid for in the same file by cutting restatement (readings under Verification).
- **Round 4, ADR-0155's second note (S1).** A second dated, append-only note follows D5. It says the switch landed before plan step 4 (#35873, on hold), which ruling 7045701086 made no prerequisite, and that seat 7's call in claim amendment 7060526112 confirmed the consequence. `driver-memory` declares no `fixedReadLeaves`, so it answers as R2: its grants go inert, stop counting and fail closed, and the grant and rule doors refuse `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` / 422. Step 4, once it lands, makes those grants count again with no change to plugin-sharing. The D5 row, Q2's closing sentence and plan step 6's "lands last" stand as written, and the note says why.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/33787-shared-record-ids-switch.md`: the three BREAKING tightenings with each host remedy, the no-object telling (plan step 1's `ISharingService` prose), the three preconditions, the cost quoted no wider than the ADR, and the PostgreSQL 16 total for a caller with no grant, measured, with follow-up #36034.

### Read first (by risk)

1. `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts`, the `shareGrantsInertReason` hunk and its two callers in `buildReadFilter` / `buildWriteFilter`. It decides whether the leaf is written at all: a wrong null writes a leaf the driver refuses with 500, a wrong reason hides every share on the object.
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts`, the first new `kernel:bootstrapped` hook, with `share-arm-boot.ts#shareGrantRegistrationRefusal`. It refuses a boot.
3. `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts`, the sharing-layer hunk (`sharesInertReason`). It changes what the explainer says admits a record.

### Two-minute check

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/shared-record-ids-switch.test.ts`. Expect `Tests 11 passed | 11 skipped (22)`: the SQLite cell runs, and the PostgreSQL cell runs too when `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` is set (then `22 passed`). The 6,000-grant pin reads 7,000 visible rows where the capped list reads 6,000.

## Tests

**D6 pins**, `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/shared-record-ids-switch.test.ts`. Real ObjectQL, the real `SqlDriver` and the real `sys_record_share`. Two cells: SQLite, and PostgreSQL 16 when `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` is set (a schema of its own, dropped after). Fixture: 1,000 owned rows, up to 6,000 granted rows (every thousandth grant read-level, the rest edit-level), a queued row, a pending-approval row, and 50 rows never admitted. Noise grants go to another user, another object, a team recipient and the agent. "Today's list" is the pre-switch read rebuilt: a system read of `sys_record_share` at `limit: 5000`, plus the approval id.

- PREMISE: the driver evaluates the leaf, and the queue arm is a real column.
- 5,000 grants, parity, every arm: leaf and today's list both count 6,002 and admit the same ids; GET by id agrees per arm (owner, queue, approval, share, plus three rows refused).
- 5,000 grants, write form: a predicate update touches the same rows through the leaf as through today's list (1,000 owned + 1 queued + 4,995 edit-level grants), never the approval row, never a read-level grant.
- 5,000 grants, nested (round 4, N4). A line item is scoped by a composed `ReadableIds` of the deal. With the leaf as the parent scope, it admits the same 6,002 lines, and the same count, as the same composition handed today's list: the `security` service gives the composition the rebuilt list instead of the sharing scope.
- 5,000 grants, delegated (round 4, N4). The agent's and the delegator's leaves, AND-ed, admit the same 150 rows as the two rebuilt lists AND-ed, and the update form touches the same 50.
- 5,001 grants: the leaf counts 6,001; today's list 6,000.
- 6,000 grants: 7,000 visible, the 6,000th granted record read by id; today's list 6,000.
- 6,000 grants, write form: 1,000 + 5,994 edit-level grants reached; today's list stops at 1,000 + 5,000.
- Nested: a line item scoped by `ReadableIds` of the deal counts 7,000, and the 6,000th grant's line is read by id.
- Delegated: the agent's and the delegator's leaves, AND-ed, admit 150; the update form touches exactly the agent's 50 edit grants.
- 6,000 grants with the queue and approval arms: 7,002, each arm its own disjunct.

**R2 and R1 pins**, `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-arm-boot.test.ts` (18 tests). R2 runs on a real ObjectQL with `SqlDriver` as the default datasource and a second datasource whose driver declares nothing. The pins cover:

- the reason, naming both datasources;
- neither scope carrying the share arm there, while the control keeps it;
- the edit gate consulting no grant;
- the grant door, as SYSTEM and as a direct caller;
- the sharing-rule save door, `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` / 422 with the remedy;
- the boot report, which names only the object holding rows, once, at `warn`, and stays silent when there are none;
- a driver beside `sys_record_share` that does not declare the leaf, named by its driver;
- an engine that cannot say, which answers null;
- the order: the storage arm is asked last, so a shipped refusal keeps its own reason.

R1:

- a clean host;
- an object-scoped middleware;
- `beforeFind` and `afterFind` hooks (one whose handler skips system reads included), each refused `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500;
- `'*'` and no-object registrations, not refused;
- a missing or throwing recognition, which warns and refuses nothing;
- a read after boot, refused `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 by the engine;
- and at the plugin: `SharingServicePlugin` through `kernel:bootstrapped` refuses a host with an `afterFind` hook for `sys_record_share`, `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 naming it, and boots a clean one.

**Explainer**, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-fixed-read-leaf.test.ts`, now on the real producer. On an object stored by a driver that does not evaluate share grants: the shares are `neutral`, the record is excluded, and the detail carries the sentence and the driver's name. On the control, the same shares admit.

**Updated for the new shape:** the plugin-sharing scope tests (`sharing-service.test.ts`, including `ctx.ast.filter` undefined on both paths) and the plugin-security tests whose doubles read the scope. Those doubles resolve the leaf through `shared-record-ids-in-memory.testkit.ts` under its own `fixedInnerReadOf`, never restating the predicate. The resolution happens where the scoped `where` reaches the double, not inside its `find` or matcher. `check:objectql-double-limit` and `check:where-matcher` lift those functions out of the file to drive them, and an imported call or a closure over the double's tables leaves them undrivable (UNJUDGED). Both gates' baselines never grow, so two doubles and one matcher were returned to their base text. The SQL-compiling tests count the semi-join: `controlled-by-parent-leaf-switch.test.ts`, and `readable-ids-nested-compose.test.ts`, which asserts no statement reads `sys_record_share` on its own.

**Ablations**, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` after committing, each restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty:

| # | Mutation | Predicted | Observed |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | the read leaf's disjunct removed from `buildReadFilter` (both cells) | read pins red; write-form and premise pins green | 12 failed, 6 passed (18) |
| 2 | the write leaf's disjunct removed from `buildWriteFilter` (SQLite) | the two write-form pins and the delegated pin red | 3 failed, 6 passed, 9 skipped (18) |
| 3 | `shareGrantsInertReason` returns null first | every R2 pin red; R1, the null answer and the silent report green | 7 failed, 10 passed (17) |
| 4 | the `kernel:bootstrapped` refusal's `throw` deleted | only the plugin-level boot pin red | 1 failed, 16 passed (17) |
| 5 | the explainer's R2 arm forced to admit | the R2 explainer pin red, its control green | 1 failed, 11 passed (12) |
| 3′ | as 3, rerun after the arm moved last | the 7 R2 pins and the order pin red | 8 failed, 10 passed (18) |
| 6 | the storage arm put back above the public check | only the order pin red | 1 failed, 17 passed (18) |
| A | round 4: the rebuilt list read at `limit: 4999` (SQLite) | read and write parity, nested parity, and the 5,001 and 6,000 list counts red; delegated parity green | 5 failed, 6 passed, 11 skipped (22): read parity, nested parity, 5,001, and both 6,000 pins. The prediction missed one pin: the 5,000 write-form pin stays green, because its list reads 4,995 edit grants, under either cap. |
| B | round 4: the rebuilt list ignores its user and reads the delegator's grants (SQLite) | only the delegated parity pin red | 1 failed, 10 passed, 11 skipped (22) |

A and B mutate the control, not the code, and show that the two new parity pins read the rebuilt list they claim to. Both ran at 4f11b215c3 and were restored to the HEAD blob (`git hash-object` equal to `HEAD:` for the file).

Ablations 1 to 5 ran before the arm moved and before both rebases; 3′ and 6 ran after the arm moved, before the second rebase. The lines they mutate are unchanged since. Ablation 3's first attempt was refused before anything ran: its replacement contained the anchor, so the anchor count could not drop. It was restored, re-anchored, and the run above is the second. The round-2 commit (28dbd3fdf1) changes prose, comments, an ADR and a skill line only, so it carries no ablation.

**Round 4, at 4f11b215c3** (this branch, the dogfood closure rebuilt first: `VERDICT command-exit 0`). PostgreSQL 16.15 ran in a private cluster for these runs and was removed after.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing typecheck`: exit 0, `check:test-typecheck: OK`.

Its checkpointer reopens `pg_control` by absolute path, and the session re-locks its scratchpad's parent directories, so the reopen was refused and the server shut down. The spec tests that read the edited files, `src/contracts/sharing-service.test.ts`, `src/data/fixed-read-leaf-conformance.test.ts` and `src/data/shared-record-ids.test.ts`: Test Files 3 passed (3), Tests 109 passed (109).

## Acceptance notes

**The dogfood `[integrity]` pin, updated.** `packages/qa/dogfood/test/authored-row-write-scope.dogfood.test.ts:284-287` pinned the bare owner match: `buildReadFilter(CLOSED, bobCtx)` toMatchObject `{ owner_id: bobId }`. Under this PR the scope is `$or` of the owner match and the leaf, so the pin went red. The next assertion (Bob reads only his own row on the private object) held throughout. The pin now asserts the owner disjunct, a one-line change and nothing else in the file (f789fb96e2):

```ts
).toMatchObject({ $or: expect.arrayContaining([{ owner_id: bobId }]) });
```

The file was outside this claim's file surface. Seat 7 asked the maintainer at 2026-11-21T09:22Z to authorize changing lines 284-287, and the maintainer (Tesla) answered verbatim at 2026-11-21T11:09:38Z: 「同意」. The file alone passes: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 12 passed (12).

**driver-memory: share grants become inert there.** driver-memory does not declare that it evaluates the share-grant leaf, so it gets R2's answer, as driver-mongodb and driver-odata do. On an object it stores, share grants stop counting: the read and update scopes fail closed to the owner, queue and approval arms, and the edit gate reads no grant. Nothing is silent about it. The grant door and the sharing-rule save door refuse a new grant or rule loudly, `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` / 422 with the reason, and the boot names, at `warn`, each such object that holds share rows. No read is refused with a 500. This is the ruled behaviour: ruling 6942854600 on #33787 (② ruled R2, the storage rows), and ADR-0111 D7's amendment note of 2026-11-17, which gives D7 this arm and says it takes effect with this switch. Seat 7 confirmed the reading on 2026-11-21. Plan step 4 (an in-process evaluation of the leaf on driver-memory) would make these grants count again with no change here. Since round 4 the record says so too: ADR-0155's second dated note, after D5 (S1). The dogfood stacks boot on sqlite-wasm, which extends `SqlDriver` and inherits its declaration, so they are not affected.

**Preconditions inherited from #35906** (close-out 7057616561), each carried into the changeset:

1. On PostgreSQL, a statement holding the leaf whose catalog read fails, or finds no such relation, answers `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500, where step 3 ran it uncast.
2. Each transaction pays one savepoint and one catalog read per table it compares a leaf against, when the table has no pooled reading.
3. A failed catalog read inside that savepoint rolls back the caller's concurrent statements on the same transaction. Read for this PR: plugin-sharing issues no statement of its own that carries the leaf (the leaf is written into the caller's `where`, and the caller's statement carries it); `sharing-service.ts` and `sharing-plugin.ts` hold 0 references to `transaction`; the plugin's own reads are sequential system reads, and its one `Promise.all` over reads (`ownership-queue-service.ts:441`) runs under the system context outside any transaction. So no producer here issues concurrent statements on one transaction while a leaf statement is primed. A caller that runs its own statements concurrently on one transaction is the precondition's case and is told in the changeset.

**The speed figure, quoted no wider than ADR-0155 "What it costs":** for the scope statements alone (the account page, its total and the two grant reads), at 1M rows and 5,000 grants, the id-list scope against the semi-join scope read PostgreSQL 21.6 → 7.0 ms and SQLite 18.3 → 12.1 ms. It is not a whole-request figure.

**The caller with no grant (D6), measured on this tree.** Before the switch the statement was the bare owner match; now it is `$or` of the owner match and the leaf. Medians of 25 runs, a page of 50 and its total, 50,000 grants held by other users, the caller holding none:

| Dialect · rows | page before → after | total before → after | Plan |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| SQLite · 100k | 1.01 → 1.09 ms | 0.08 → 0.13 ms | MULTI-INDEX OR: `idx_..._owner_id` kept on page and total |
| SQLite · 1M | 5.85 → 7.36 ms | 0.28 → 0.60 ms | same |
| PostgreSQL 16 · 100k | 1.59 → 1.72 ms | 1.46 → 7.29 ms | page: pkey index scan both; total: Bitmap on `idx_..._owner_id` → Seq Scan with a hashed SubPlan |
| PostgreSQL 16 · 1M | 1.65 → 1.58 ms | 7.88 → 42.21 ms | total: Parallel Seq Scan |

SQLite still serves both from the owner index. PostgreSQL serves the page as before but plans the total as a sequential scan, which grows with the table; this agrees with step 3's reading (close-out 7048322381), whose L2 named `id = ANY(ARRAY(SELECT ...))` as an alternative. The cost ships stated in the changeset and the 速读 (seat 7's call, 2026-11-21); follow-up #36034 measures that form against the semi-join for this caller on PostgreSQL. It is named here as a cost, not changed.

**O8 census, this repository at 8c8ff0f25d.** No site changes a system read of `sys_record_share`; no registration names it by name; no default opts it into record-view auditing. No D-0 finding.
